nodes.summary: For every finite measurable partition `ξ` indexed by `Fin r`, `h_μ(T, ξ) ≤ h_μ(T)`.
nodes.title: Relative entropy is bounded by the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy

nodes.summary: If `π : (α, μ) → (β, ν)` is measure-preserving, `T` is quasi-measure-preserving, `S` is measurable and `π ∘ T = S ∘ π` almost everywhere, then `h_μ(T, π⁻¹η) = h_ν(S, η)` for every finite measurable partition `η` of `β`.
nodes.title: Relative entropy of a pulled-back partition under an a.e. factor map

nodes.summary: If `π : (α, μ, T) → (β, ν, S)` is measure-preserving with `π ∘ T = S ∘ π`, then `h_μ(T, π⁻¹η) = h_ν(S, η)` for every finite measurable partition `η` of `β`: the two refinements have atoms of equal measure.
nodes.title: Relative entropy of a pulled-back partition

nodes.summary: For the Bernoulli shift $\sigma$ with distribution $p$ on a finite alphabet $S$ and the time-zero partition $\xi$, By the entropy of the refined time-zero partition, the sequence $\frac1n H(\xi \vee \dots \vee \sigma^{-(n-1)}\xi)$ is constant, equal to $H(p)$, for $n \ge 1$, so its limit is $H(p)$.
nodes.title: Entropy of the Bernoulli shift relative to the time-zero partition

The value is taken in $[0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Entropy of a transformation relative to a partition

nodes.summary: Under `p^ℕ`, the cylinder of the word `w : Fin n → S` has measure `p {w 0} ⋯ p {w (n-1)}`.
nodes.title: Measure of a cylinder under a product measure

nodes.summary: A conjugacy by a measure-preserving measurable equivalence is an isomorphism modulo null sets.
nodes.title: A conjugacy by a measure-preserving measurable equivalence is an isomorphism modulo null sets

nodes.summary: Two dynamical systems $(X, \mu, T)$ and $(Y, \nu, S)$ are *isomorphic modulo null sets* if there are measure-preserving maps $\pi : X \to Y$ and $\rho : Y \to X$ such that
nodes.title: Isomorphism modulo null sets

nodes.summary: The time-zero partition is a measurable partition of the shift space, for any measure.
nodes.title: The time-zero partition is a measurable partition

nodes.summary: A family `ξ : ι → Set α` of measurable sets is a measurable partition of `(α, μ)` if its members are pairwise disjoint up to `μ`-null sets and cover `α` up to a `μ`-null set.
nodes.title: Finite measurable partition modulo null sets

nodes.summary: If `T` is quasi-measure-preserving and `π ∘ T = S ∘ π` almost everywhere, then `π ∘ T^[k] = S^[k] ∘ π` almost everywhere.
nodes.title: Almost-everywhere semiconjugacy passes to iterates

nodes.summary: If `T` is quasi-measure-preserving and `π ∘ T = S ∘ π` almost everywhere, then each atom of the refinement of `π⁻¹η` under `T` agrees almost everywhere with the preimage under `π` of the corresponding atom of the refinement of `η` under `S`.
nodes.title: Dynamical refinement commutes with pullback, almost everywhere

nodes.summary: If `π ∘ T = S ∘ π`, the atom of the word `w` in the refinement of the pulled-back partition `π⁻¹η` under `T` is the preimage under `π` of the atom of `w` in the refinement of `η` under `S`.
nodes.title: Dynamical refinement commutes with pullback along a factor map

nodes.summary: The atom of the word `w : Fin n → S` in `ξ ∨ σ⁻¹ξ ∨ ⋯ ∨ σ^{-(n-1)}ξ` is the cylinder `{x | x k = w k for k < n}`.
nodes.title: Refinements of the time-zero partition are cylinders

nodes.summary: The partition `ξ ∨ T⁻¹ξ ∨ ⋯ ∨ T^{-(n-1)}ξ`, indexed by words `w : Fin n → ι`: the atom of `w` is the set of points `x` with `T^[k] x ∈ ξ (w k)` for every `k < n`, i.e. the points whose `ξ`-itinerary begins with `w`.
nodes.title: Dynamical refinement of a partition

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be irrational. The rotation $x \mapsto x + \alpha$ of the circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, with its Haar probability measure (Lebesgue measure), has Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy $0$.
nodes.title: The irrational rotation has entropy zero

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite alphabet with its discrete σ-algebra and $p$ a probability vector on $S$. The Bernoulli scheme with probability vector $p$, the left shift on $S^{\mathbb{N}}$ with the product measure $p^{\mathbb{N}}$, has Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy
nodes.title: Entropy of a Bernoulli shift

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an invertible measure-preserving transformation of a probability space $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$, and let $\xi = \{C_1, \dots, C_r\}$ be a finite measurable partition which is a *generator*: the smallest σ-algebra containing all the sets $T^n C_j$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, $1 \le j \le r$, is $\mathcal{B}$ modulo $\mu$-null sets. Then
nodes.title: Sinai's generator theorem

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a measure-preserving transformation of a probability space $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$, not necessarily invertible, and let $\xi = \{C_1, \dots, C_r\}$ be a finite measurable partition which is a *strong generator*: the σ-algebra generated by the sets $T^{-i} C_j$, $i \ge 0$, is $\mathcal{B}$ modulo $\mu$. Then $h_\mu(T) = h_\mu(T, \xi)$.
nodes.title: Sinai's generator theorem, noninvertible case

nodes.summary: If two measure-preserving systems $(X, \mu, T)$ and $(Y, \nu, S)$ are isomorphic modulo null sets, then $h_\mu(T) = h_\nu(S)$.
nodes.title: Entropy is an invariant of isomorphism modulo null sets

nodes.summary: For every measure space $(X, \mu)$, the identity map has Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy $h_\mu(\mathrm{id}) = 0$.
nodes.title: The identity has zero entropy

nodes.summary: If `π : (α, μ) → (β, ν)` is measure-preserving, `T` is quasi-measure-preserving, `S` is measurable and `π ∘ T = S ∘ π` almost everywhere, then `h_ν(S) ≤ h_μ(T)`.
nodes.title: Entropy does not increase under factors (almost-everywhere form)

nodes.summary: If `π` is a measure-preserving map from `(α, μ, T)` onto `(β, ν, S)` with `π ∘ T = S ∘ π`, then `h_ν(S) ≤ h_μ(T)`: every finite partition of the factor pulls back to a partition of the system with the same relative entropy (cf. O. Sarig, *Lecture Notes on Ergodic Theory*, §4.3).
nodes.title: Entropy does not increase under factors

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a measurable map of a measure space $(X, \mu)$. The Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of $T$ is the supremum, over all finite measurable partitions $\xi$ of $X$, of the entropy of $T$ relative to $\xi$. It takes values in $[0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy

nodes.summary: If `T` is measurable and every atom of `ξ` is measurable, then every atom of `ξ ∨ T⁻¹ξ ∨ ⋯ ∨ T^{-(n-1)}ξ` is measurable.
nodes.title: Atoms of the dynamical refinement are measurable

nodes.summary: The Bernoulli schemes with probability vectors $(\tfrac13, \tfrac13, \tfrac13)$ and $(\tfrac12, \tfrac12)$ are not measure-theoretically isomorphic, even modulo null sets: no pair of measure-preserving maps, inverse to each other almost everywhere, intertwines the two shifts almost everywhere. Their entropies are $\log 3$ and $\log 2$.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov's non-isomorphism of Bernoulli schemes

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite alphabet with its discrete σ-algebra and $p$ a probability vector on $S$. The Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of the Bernoulli shift with distribution $p$ satisfies In particular a Bernoulli shift whose distribution is not a point mass has positive entropy, which is how entropy separates "probabilistic" systems from those of entropy zero.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the entropy of a Bernoulli shift

nodes.summary: Let $S$ and $S'$ be finite alphabets with probability vectors $p$ and $q$. If the two-sided Bernoulli shifts on $S^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $S'^{\mathbb{Z}}$, with product measures $p^{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $q^{\mathbb{Z}}$, have the same Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, then they are isomorphic modulo null sets: there are measure-preserving maps in both directions, inverse to each other almost everywhere, that intertwine the two…
nodes.title: Ornstein's isomorphism theorem

nodes.summary: For the identity map and `n ≥ 1`, the dynamical refinement `ξ ∨ ξ ∨ ⋯ ∨ ξ` of a measurable partition has the same entropy as `ξ`: the atom of a constant word `(i, …, i)` is `ξ i`, and the atom of a non-constant word is contained in the intersection of two distinct atoms, a null set.
nodes.title: Refinements under the identity

nodes.summary: For the Bernoulli shift $\sigma$ with distribution $p$ on a finite alphabet $S$ and the time-zero partition $\xi = \{[s] : s \in S\}$, H(p) = -\sum_{s} p(s) \log p(s).$$ The atoms of the refinement are the cylinders of length $n$, of measure $p(w_0) \cdots p(w_{n-1})$, and the entropy of $n$ independent letters is $n$ times the entropy of one.
nodes.title: Entropy of the refined time-zero partition

nodes.summary: Entropy of a partition is nonnegative for a probability measure, since every atom has measure in `[0, 1]` and `-t log t ≥ 0` there.
nodes.title: Entropy of a partition is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a finite family $\xi = (C_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets in a measure space $(X, \mu)$, its entropy is with the convention $0 \log 0 = 0$. For a partition of a probability space this is the Shannon entropy of the probability vector $(\mu(C_i))_i$, the average information gained by learning which atom contains a random point. The logarithm is natural, as in Sinai's article; Sarig uses $\log_2$, which divides every…
nodes.title: Entropy of a finite partition

nodes.summary: The preimages `π⁻¹ ηᵢ` of the atoms of a measurable partition `η` of `(β, ν)` under a measure-preserving map `π : (α, μ) → (β, ν)` form a measurable partition of `(α, μ)`.
nodes.title: Pullback of a measurable partition

nodes.summary: If `a : S → ℝ` is a probability vector, then `∑_{w ∈ Sⁿ} negMulLog (a(w₀) ⋯ a(w_{n-1})) = n · ∑_s negMulLog (a s)`: the entropy of `n` independent letters is `n` times the entropy of one.
nodes.title: Entropy of a product distribution on words

nodes.summary: The partition of `ℕ → S` into the cylinders `[s] = {x | x 0 = s}`, `s ∈ S`, according to the symbol at time `0`.
